title: Practice: Design a Parking Lot
summary: Run the whole interview yourself, one step at a time: clarify, model, diagram, park/unpark flows, pricing and allocation strategies, concurrency, code and follow-ups.

steps.title: Clarify the requirements
hints: Group your questions: **what** gets parked, **how** spots are chosen, **how** money works, **how many** gates.
Ask about *scope* explicitly too: payments, reservations, persistence, UI. Saying "out of scope" out loud is a signal of seniority.
checklist: Vehicle types and spot sizes, and which fits where
Multiple floors and multiple entry/exit gates
How a ticket is issued and how the fee is computed
How a spot is chosen (and that it should be swappable)
A short, explicit out-of-scope list

steps.title: Identify entities and enums
hints: Underline the nouns in your requirements. Each is a class, an enum, a field or noise.
Ask yourself: does `Car` behave differently from `Truck`, or does it just have different data?
checklist: Enums for VehicleType and SpotSize (not a Car/Truck class hierarchy)
Spot, Floor (or just a floor number), Ticket, Receipt
A ParkingLot facade that owns the spots
Interfaces for what varies: pricing and spot selection

steps.title: Draw the class diagram
hints: Start from the facade (`ParkingLot`) and draw what it owns (composition) versus what it uses (association).
Put the interfaces on the diagram with their single method. That's what interviewers look for.
checklist: ParkingLot composes spots; spots are not shared
PricingStrategy and SpotSelector as interfaces with implementations
Ticket and Receipt as immutable value objects
Multiplicities on the main relationships

steps.title: Walk through park() and unpark()
hints: List the failure cases first: no fitting spot, plate already inside, unknown or reused ticket.
Which maps do you need for O(1) unpark? Think ticketId → ?, plate → ?
checklist: park: reject duplicate plate, select spot, occupy, issue ticket
unpark: look up ticket, compute fee, free the spot, remove the ticket
An index from ticket id to ticket/spot, and a set of plates inside
Clock is injected so time-based fees are testable

steps.title: Make it extensible: pricing, allocation, display board
hints: Which three things will the interviewer ask you to change? Each one becomes a seam.
The display board must not be polled. Who should tell it that a spot changed?
checklist: Strategy for pricing (hourly, flat, weekend…)
Strategy for spot selection (nearest, fill-top-first, EV-first…)
Observer for display boards and other listeners
Open/Closed: new behaviour = new class, no edits to ParkingLot

steps.title: Concurrency and edge cases
hints: Two gates call `park()` at the same instant and both see spot F1-M1 free. What happens?
Compare one lock for the whole lot vs. a lock per floor vs. compare-and-set per spot.
checklist: The check-then-act race on spot selection is named
A concrete fix (lot lock, per-floor lock or CAS on the spot) with trade-offs
Listeners notified outside the lock
Edge cases: lost ticket, double unpark, lot full, clock skew

steps.title: Code the core
hints: Write the interfaces first, then `Spot`, then `ParkingLot`. Leave `main` and printing for last (or skip them).
checklist: Compiles in your language, with enums and interfaces
park/unpark with the failure cases from step 4
Strategies injected through the constructor
A lock (or equivalent) around the state that changes

steps.title: Answer the follow-ups
hints: For each follow-up say *which class changes* and *which doesn't*. That is the whole point of the question.
It's fine to say "that needs persistence, so this becomes a service with a DB". Just say where the boundary is.
checklist: EV charging spots without touching existing selectors
Reservations / pre-booking
Multiple lots / horizontal scaling
Payment methods and failed payments
